title: Progressive windowed telemetry, adaptive sampling, and privacy buckets for streamed outputs
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background:
Redwood streaming endpoints produce high-cardinality incremental outputs. Current telemetry creates either too many spans or too coarse metrics, which makes diagnosing per-chunk latency regressions and privacy leaks difficult. We need a flexible telemetry layer that reduces noise, captures per-window performance, preserves provenance for tool/function calls, and enforces deterministic redaction for sensitive tokens in logs.

Goals:
- Provide progressive, sliding-window telemetry that emits summary metrics at configurable window sizes (e.g., 50ms, 250ms, 1s) while still allowing per-chunk histograms on demand.
- Implement adaptive sampling tied to session and error signals to increase fidelity when clients experience issues (e.g., high latency, tool call failures).
- Introduce "privacy buckets": sensitivity classification applied at token/window boundaries that drives log redaction granularity and storage retention.
- Reduce tracing span explosion by coalescing short-lived chunk spans into a small set of semantic spans (generation-window, tool-call, flush) while preserving trace links for debugging.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not change existing public API payloads or client SDK contracts.
- Not responsible for storage/perf optimizations of long-term telemetry retention beyond retention policy flags.

Proposed approach:
1. Telemetry windows: implement a windowing layer in the streaming runtime that aggregates per-token metrics into configurable buckets and emits both aggregate counters and sampled per-chunk histograms when the adaptive sampler triggers.
2. Adaptive sampler: a probabilistic sampler whose base probability is governed by rate limits and can be boosted by signals: per-session error rate, SLA breach, customer debug flag, or explicit SDK header (x-rw-debug).
3. Privacy buckets: during tokenization, annotate tokens with sensitivity scores (none, low, medium, high) via a lightweight regexp + rule table. Windows inherit the highest sensitivity bucket among tokens they contain; redaction rules and retention TTL are selected by bucket.
4. Span coalescing: runtime creates short local spans per-chunk but merges consecutive chunk spans within a window into a single parent span for exported traces. Exported spans include a per-window token_count, kv_cache_hits, and tool_call_count. Full per-chunk spans are stored only when sampling triggers.
5. Export pipeline: add a new telemetry tag set: window_size_ms, sample_reason, privacy_bucket, session_id, route, model_version, dedupe_key. Integrate with existing flamegraph/tracing dashboards and add new Grafana panels.

Telemetry schema (examples):
- metric:stream.window.latency.p50{window_size_ms=250,route="text.generate",model="rw-13b"}
- metric:stream.window.tokens.count{window_size_ms=250,privacy_bucket="low"}
- trace span:stream.window{duration_ms=1200,token_count=340,kv_cache_hit_ratio=0.72,sample_reason="error_boost"}

Acceptance criteria (high-level):
- Runtime emits windowed metrics at configured sizes and these appear in internal metrics store (observability team validates).
- Adaptive sampler can be toggled per-customer and boosts sampling on error conditions.
- Privacy buckets applied correctly on a representative corpus (unit test corpus + synthetic PII cases).
- Span coalescing reduces exported span count by >= 60% on high-throughput streams while retaining ability to link to sampled per-chunk spans.
- Documentation updated: design doc, SDK debug header docs, and Console feature doc for new observability panels.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): enable windowed metrics (non-redaction) for internal traffic and 5 internal customers. Monitor metric correctness and performance.
- Phase 2 (private beta): enable adaptive sampling and span coalescing with privacy buckets for select customers; collect privacy-bucket distribution and retention effects.
- Phase 3 (general availability): enable defaults with safe conservative sampling and redaction rules; expose configuration knobs in Dedicated and Private.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Token sensitivity misclassification causing over-redaction. Mitigation: conservative default rules, opt-in aggressive rules, and a review checklist with Security.
- Risk: Increased CPU in runtime for windowing. Mitigation: benchmark CPU impact in canary and add circuit breaker thresholds.
- Risk: Trace linking complexity. Mitigation: deterministic span ids and dedupe_key inclusion in exported spans.

Dependencies:
acceptance_criteria: Windowed metrics are visible in metrics store for 50ms/250ms/1s windows.
Adaptive sampler reacts to session error rate and increases sample probability by at least 10x during detected incidents.
Privacy buckets classification unit tests cover 200+ PII regex rules and pass.
Exported span volume reduced by >=60% under synthetic high-throughput workload while sampled per-chunk traces remain linkable.
Console shows new panels and a toggle to enable per-route sampling overrides.
implementation_notes: Add a memory-bounded circular buffer per stream to accumulate window aggregates.
Implement sampler as an injectable strategy with validators for per-customer overrides.
Store sampled per-chunk payload references in a short-lived store (48h) with a dedupe_key to avoid duplicates.
Expose telemetry knobs via runtime-config with safe defaults and feature flags.
testing_plan: Unit tests for privacy bucket classification and window aggregation logic.
Load test with synthetic streams at 5k req/s verifying CPU and memory impact.
End-to-end trace tests ensuring span linkage from coalesced windows to sampled chunk traces.
Privacy compliance review with Security and Legal for retention TTLs.
